# Plan: move system-assembly codegen from the CLI into the template library

Audience: the agent implementing this change. Read the referenced files
before writing code; they are the ground truth where this plan and the code
disagree.

## Goal

`intropy sys create` today renders the `system-host` template shell and then
**the CLI itself** writes all C# declaration files, edits the csproj, and
creates connector test folders. The CLI thereby encodes the Intropy.Topology
API surface, csproj XML, and three branches of "template release era"
detection. Every Intropy.Topology API change currently forces a CLI release.

After this change:

- The **template library** owns every byte of C# and .NET project content:
  `Topics.cs`, `Connectors.cs`, `<ProjectName>Development.cs`,
  `<SystemClass>.cs`, the csproj `<ProjectReference>` to the contracts
  project, and the default extractor schedule.
- The **CLI** owns only workspace knowledge: scanning scaffold records,
  topology validation (duplicates, conflicts, exactly-one-shared-library),
  path computation, and assembling a structured value payload passed to one
  `template.Create` call.
- Template version = Intropy.Topology version = generated code shape, one
  atomic unit. All era/degrade logic is deleted.

## Compatibility stance: none

Everything here is **preview**. Keep nothing for backwards compatibility:

- Delete the era/degrade branches outright (they already only existed to
  paper over the split-brain). No deprecation window, no fallback path.
- Old CLI + new template and new CLI + old template are both unsupported
  combinations that must **fail fast with a remedy in the message**. There
  is no supported mixed-version matrix to design for.
- The flag surface, result JSON shape, scaffold.json schema, and payload
  contract may all change freely if the implementation lands somewhere
  better than this plan's sketches. This plan describes intent and
  constraints, not frozen shapes.
- Existing workspaces simply re-run `sys create` with a matched CLI and
  template release; there is no migration path to build.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **The .slnx solution file.** Deferred. It is the only artifact that would
  need rendering outside the host output dir (workspace root), which would
  force a new render-engine concept (`ExtraRenders`). It lands as a
  follow-up once this change has shipped. Do not add `ExtraRenders` or any
  workspace-root rendering in this work.
- Changing `int create`, component templates' rendered output, or the
  scaffold.json schema. (One optional, additive exception: see "Preserve
  slnx optionality" below.)
- Changing the flag surface, result JSON schema, or `template.Create`'s
  public contract beyond what this plan states.

## Architecture facts the implementation must respect

apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: system-host
  title: System Host
  description: The Aspire host project of an Intropy integration system. Declares the system's components and the edges between them as one typed C# declaration, validates the topology, and runs or generates the system from the same model. Renders every declaration file from the value payload `intropy sys create` assembles; without that payload it renders a valid empty system.
  tags:
    - dotnet
    - aspire
    - system
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: example
    intropy.dev/template-role: system-host

spec:
  # `intropy sys create` renders this template with the full value payload
  # and --no-input. The payload parameters are required so an older CLI
  # that only sets `name` fails validation loudly instead of rendering an
  # empty system. They are supplied programmatically — never via --set or
  # prompts — so they carry no title/description.
  parameters:
    type: object
    required:
      - name
      - topics
      - connectors
      - components
      - sharedContracts
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: System name
        description: DNS-1123 name of the integration system (e.g. order-flow). Becomes the SystemName. The pub/sub component is always named `pubsub` (system-independent), so a component runs the same standalone or under this host.
        pattern: "^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$"
      # The payload below. The CLI pre-joins every reference (each
      # component carries the Topics/Connectors field identifiers it
      # touches), so the skeleton is a flat range over these lists — no
      # lookups. Empty lists render a valid empty system, so no minItems.
      topics:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
      connectors:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
      components:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
      sharedContracts:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: true
  values:
    # Must match the CLI's pascalCase(name): the CLI's payload assembly
    # derives the same project name for its result summary, and a
    # derivation that disagrees renders files under names the CLI's
    # summary does not report.
    projectName: '{{ .name | replace "-" " " | title | replace " " "" }}'
    systemClass: '{{ .name | replace "-" " " | title | replace " " "" }}System'
    pubsub: 'pubsub'

# Plan: track Intropy.Topology 0.4.0 ("minted facts") in the CLI

## What changed upstream

**Intropy.Topology 0.3.4 → 0.4.0** (two breaking commits):
- `7cea328` — the connector **transport is deleted** from the model. `ConnectorRef.Define(name)`; the graph JSON no longer emits `transport` or `deployedTransport` on connectors. The name is the connector's whole identity.
- `dba0262` — the **schedule is deleted**. `ExtractorBuilder.WithSchedule` and `ComponentModel.Schedule` gone; the deployed CronJob cadence lives in the GitOps repo (environment-owned).

**intropy-templates** already tracked this:
- `system-host` (`13844c8`): name-only connectors, no `.WithSchedule`, **`extractorSchedule` parameter removed from template.yaml**.
- `deploy-host` (`f83b424`): `.topology.connectors` entries arrive **without transport**; bindings render as REPLACE-ME scaffolds owned by GitOps.

## CLI delta (current state)

The `feature/template-owns-codegen` work already landed, so `sys create` no longer sends `extractorSchedule` or any transport-shaped value — that path is clean. The drift is concentrated in the graph-record consumer side:

1. **`internal/topology/topology.go`** — `Connector.Transport` is a required `Transport` struct, `DeployedTransport *Transport` still parsed, doc comments describe transports as lookup-table metadata. `topology_test.go` asserts all of it.
2. **`internal/deploy/initmodel.go`** — `InitConnector.Transport string` and `buildConnectors` preferring `DeployedTransport` over `Transport`. This is the injected `.topology` the deploy-host skeleton ranges over — the template no longer reads `.transport`, so the key is dead weight that will silently render empty against 0.4.0 hosts.
3. **`internal/deploy/localtemplates_test.go`** — golden test asserting deployed-transport binding rendering (`bindings.sftp`, no `bindings.localstorage`).
4. **`internal/deploy/initmodel_test.go`** — `TestInitModelConnectorsPreferDeployedTransport` and transport assertions.
5. **`internal/dashboard/dashboard_test.go:385`** — fixture constructs `topology.Transport{...}`.
6. **Stale `create_test.go` goldens** — `internal/system/create_test.go` still references `extractorSchedule` / `.WithSchedule(...)` in rendered-file fixtures (flagged by the topology repo itself at `428e3fb`).

## Work items (in order)

### 1. `internal/topology`: decode name-only connectors
- Remove `Transport` struct, `Connector.Transport`, `Connector.DeployedTransport`.
- Rewrite package/type doc comments: connectors are minted names; binding type is environment-owned deployment configuration.
- Keep decode tolerance note: unknown fields are ignored by `encoding/json`, so a 0.3.x record still decodes — decide explicitly whether that's acceptable (silently dropping transport) or whether to reject old records. Recommendation: accept and ignore; the apiVersion is unchanged (`topology.intropy.io/v1`) and the CLI's failure mode should be the deploy-host template's, not the decoder's. Document this in the `Decode` comment.
- Rewrite `topology_test.go`: name-only connector decode; drop the two deployed-transport tests.

### 2. `internal/deploy`: drop transport from the injected topology model
- `initmodel.go`: remove `InitConnector.Transport`; `buildConnectors` reduces to name/externalSystem/directions/appIds. Update the `InitConnector` doc comment (the "no address, host or credential" rationale now covers the type too).
- `initmodel_test.go`: remove `TestInitModelConnectorsPreferDeployedTransport`, transport assertions, and transport fields from fixtures.
- `localtemplates_test.go`: replace `TestLocalTemplatesRenderDeployedTransportBinding` with a test asserting the REPLACE-ME binding scaffold (name + scopes minted, `REPLACE-ME-BINDING-TYPE` present, no transport switch). Requires refreshing the embedded/local deploy-host template copy the test renders against.
- Verify no other code path reads `.topology.connectors[].transport` (grep confirms only the above).

### 3. `internal/dashboard`: fix fixture, check render surface
- `dashboard_test.go:385`: drop the `Transport:` field from the fixture connector.
- Check whether the dashboard UI surfaces connector transport anywhere (frontend/templates). If it does, remove that display — the fact no longer exists.

### 4. `internal/system`: refresh create goldens
- `create_test.go` fixtures: drop `extractorSchedule` from recorded values, `.WithSchedule(...)` from rendered C# expectations. Assert the payload does **not** contain `extractorSchedule`.
- Confirm `sys create` works end-to-end against the new `system-host` template release (render a fixture workspace; compile would be ideal but a golden-file diff is the minimum).

### 5. Help text / docs sweep
- `cmd/intropy/deploy_init.go` long text already says cron schedules are placeholders — still accurate, keep.
- `internal/deploy/initmodel.go` header comment ("An extractor is scheduled…") is about the CronJob workload convention, which survives; light touch-up only.
- No vocabulary additions needed in AGENTS.md.

### 6. Version floor
- The deploy-host/system-host templates now require 0.4.0 packages. Consider whether the CLI should warn when a scaffold record's template version predates the 0.4.0-tracking template release. Recommendation: no new gate — the template's csproj pin and the graph decode are the enforcement points; keep the CLI version-agnostic.

## Out of scope
- No changes to `sys create` payload assembly, flag surface, or scaffold.json schema (already transport/schedule-free).
